description: A small curated benchmark for validating Breach's claim-verification pipeline against real, externally-sourced mathematical statements rather than only self-authored test cases.

sources.name: miniF2F
sources.citation: Zheng, Han, Polu. 'miniF2F: a cross-system benchmark for formal Olympiad-level mathematics.' arXiv:2109.00110

sources.name: Historical false conjectures
sources.citation: Used for narrative/context entries only; not run as executable test cases unless noted.

scope_note: Breach verifies bounded, mechanically-decidable claims via Z3/SymPy. Entries are selected from miniF2F specifically where they fall inside this scope (algebraic identities, bounded number theory), not from miniF2F's full formal-proof-construction split, which is out of scope by design (see README).

cases.name: amc12_2000_p11
cases.claim_nl: for nonzero reals a and b, if a*b = a - b, then a/b + b/a - a*b = 2
cases.command: breach check "for nonzero reals a and b, if a*b = a - b, then a/b + b/a - a*b = 2"
cases.ground_truth_method: verified independently via SymPy symbolic simplification
cases.known_limitation: Breach's current translator may encode this as a bounded numeric search (e.g. reals in [-10,10]) rather than recognizing it as symbolically provable via SymPy. The verdict is still correct; the proof strength is weaker than it could be. Tracked as a known improvement area.

cases.name: mathd_numbertheory_618
cases.claim_nl: for positive integer n, let p(n) = n^2 - n + 41; if gcd(p(n), p(n+1)) > 1 then n >= 41
cases.command: breach check "for positive integer n, let p(n) = n^2 - n + 41; if gcd(p(n), p(n+1)) > 1 then n >= 41"
cases.ground_truth_method: first witness independently confirmed at n = 41
cases.known_limitation: Initial testing found this translation non-deterministic across repeated runs (sometimes unknown/translation_ambiguity, sometimes unknown/timeout, sometimes correct). Root cause: no validation/retry when the LLM-generated solver encoding fails to parse. Fixed by adding translation validation with automatic retry on parse failure (see CHANGELOG). Re-verified deterministic post-fix.

cases.name: mathd_algebra_487
cases.claim_nl: for the two intersection points of y = x^2 and x + y = 1 (with a != c), the distance between them is sqrt(10)
cases.command: breach check "if a^2 = b, a + b = 1, c^2 = d, c + d = 1, and a != c, then sqrt((a-c)^2 + (b-d)^2) = sqrt(10)"
cases.known_limitation: Correct across all test runs; bound margin was tight in one encoding ([-2,2], against true roots at approx 0.618 and -1.618) — flagged for future tightening of default bounds.

cases.name: polya_conjecture_1919
cases.source: Historical reference only — not executed as a Breach test case
cases.claim_nl: The Polya conjecture (summatory Liouville function parity)
cases.ground_truth: FALSE (first counterexample at n = 906,150,257, found by C.B. Haselgrove, 1958)
cases.known_limitation: Included for narrative/scale context only (illustrates the real-world scale of 'held true for decades, later falsified' claims). Breach has NOT found or verified this counterexample — it is roughly 4 orders of magnitude beyond laptop-scale search. Independently confirmed no counterexample exists below n = 200,000 within this project's own testing. Must not be represented as a Breach result.

cases.name: control_false_inequality
cases.source: Authored for this corpus as a control case, styled after miniF2F algebra entries
cases.claim_nl: for all positive integers a and b, a^2 + b^2 >= 2*a*b + 1
cases.command: breach check "for all positive integers a and b, a^2 + b^2 >= 2*a*b + 1"
cases.ground_truth_method: direct substitution, e.g. a=b=1 gives 2 >= 3, false
cases.known_limitation: None observed; stable across all test runs. Included to confirm the counterexample-finding path works correctly on a realistic-looking but false claim, not only on true claims.

cases.name: mathd_algebra_141
cases.claim_nl: for real numbers a and b, if a*b = 180 and a + b = 27, then a^2 + b^2 = 369
cases.command: breach check "for real numbers a and b, if a*b = 180 and a + b = 27, then a^2 + b^2 = 369"
cases.ground_truth_method: verified independently via algebraic identity: a^2+b^2 = (a+b)^2 - 2ab = 27^2 - 2*180 = 729 - 360 = 369

cases.name: mathd_algebra_160

cases.ground_truth_method: solving the linear system: from n+x=97 and n+5x=265, subtracting gives 4x=168, x=42, n=55, then n+2x=55+84=139

results_summary.notes: BVC-002 was flaky on first pass (translation non-determinism); root-caused and fixed by adding encoding validation with retry-on-parse-failure. Re-verified deterministic after the fix. All other runnable cases passed consistently across repeated runs.

accuracy.note: Small sample: this is a 4-case corpus, so the overall figure is a smoke-test signal, not a benchmark score. Breach never returned a confident wrong verdict - failures surfaced as an honest 'unknown'.
